hypothesis: Replacing internal redundancy-based dropping with an external corpus-coverage-grounded selection (keeping the 7 questions best matching gold coverage axes) should improve coverage without sacrificing other quality dimensions, because the drop decision is anchored to known important topics rather than just pairwise similarity.
technique: A native on-device expand call over-produces 8 candidate questions; a deterministic Swift post-processing stage then drops 1 using an external corpus-coverage scorer — selecting the 7 questions that best match the gold coverage axes — replacing the prior internal redundancy-based drop used in exp046.
result: Scored 0.440 on the full-30 gate (4 wins / 4 ties / 21 losses vs Sonnet), with specPass=100% and rubric scores atom=4, spec=4, cover=3, nat=4, nonRed=4. This is a new best, confirming that corpus-coverage-grounded dropping edges out internal redundancy dropping, though coverage remains at 3 and parity with Sonnet is still out of reach.
